programs.name: South Carolina Department on Aging (State Unit on Aging)
programs.federal_name: Older Americans Act Title III-B / III-E (Area Agencies on Aging)
programs.about: South Carolina's state unit on aging funds local Area Agencies on Aging. Your local Area Agency on Aging may help with a home safety check or small changes; find it through the Eldercare Locator.

programs.name: South Carolina Assistive Technology Program
programs.about: South Carolina's federally funded assistive technology program; some AT programs help with home changes or link people to low-cost loans.

programs.name: South Carolina Centers for Independent Living
programs.about: Independent living centers in South Carolina give advice, skills training and referrals to people with disabilities; some help pay for home changes.

programs.name: VA Specially Adapted Housing (SAH), Special Housing Adaptation (SHA), Temporary Residence Adaptation (TRA) and HISA grants
programs.federal_name: VA SAH / SHA / TRA / HISA grants

programs.name: South Carolina Vocational Rehabilitation Department
programs.about: South Carolina Vocational Rehabilitation Department may pay for home changes or devices when they help a person with a disability reach a job goal.

programs.name: Insurance: Health (e.g., Medicare) and HMOs, Long-Term Care, Life
programs.federal_name: Medicare / Medicare Advantage and private insurance

programs.name: South Carolina Medicaid, Health Connections
programs.about: South Carolina Medicaid, Health Connections runs South Carolina's Medicaid home and community-based waivers. Some waivers pay for home changes (often called environmental modifications) so a person with low income who needs long-term care can stay home. The USC SC state profile summarizes which waivers cover this.

programs.name: South Carolina Money Follows the Person Program, Home Again
programs.about: South Carolina's Money Follows the Person program, Home Again, helps people with disabilities or chronic conditions move from a nursing home or institution back to a home in the community.

programs.name: Social Security: Plan for Achieving Self-Support (PASS) and Impairment-Related Work Expenses (IRWE)
programs.about: Work rules for people on SSI or SSDI. They can set money aside or subtract disability-related work costs, which may include home changes, so their benefits drop less.

programs.name: Community Development Block Grants (CDBG): State CDBG Program and CDBG Entitlement Program
HOME Program (local HOME grantees)
Local Housing/Neighborhood Agencies (Neighborhood Housing Services)
programs.about: Local nonprofit housing groups, such as NeighborWorks affiliates, may give repair advice, loans or grants. Search the NeighborWorks directory or your city name plus "Neighborhood Housing Services" to find groups in South Carolina.

programs.name: South Carolina Housing, Finance, and Development Authority
programs.about: South Carolina Housing, Finance, and Development Authority is South Carolina's housing finance agency. HFAs mostly fund home buying and affordable housing, and some offer low-interest or deferred repair loans. Check its site for any current repair or accessibility program.

programs.name: South Carolina USDA Rural Development offices
programs.federal_name: USDA Section 504 Home Repair loans and grants; Section 533 Housing Preservation Grants
programs.about: Rural South Carolina homeowners with very low income can contact the USDA Rural Development state office about 504 repair loans and grants.

programs.name: South Carolina Weatherization Assistance Program
programs.about: Lowers energy bills for lower-income South Carolina households and can include small health and safety repairs.

programs.name: FHA Loan Insurance: Title I Home Improvement and 203(k) Purchase/Rehabilitation
Home Equity Line of Credit
programs.about: A credit line borrowed against the home's value that can be drawn on as needed for home changes. It is repaid with interest. Ask a local bank or credit union.

programs.name: Home Equity Loan
programs.about: A second mortgage that pays out a lump sum for home changes and is repaid on top of the first mortgage. Ask a local bank.

programs.name: Lender Unsecured/Personal Loans
programs.about: A personal loan from a bank puts no lien on the home, so it can work for renters and smaller projects. Approval depends on income, debt and credit.

programs.name: Civic, Advocacy, Religious, and Trade Groups
programs.about: Churches, service clubs, trade unions and builder groups sometimes run volunteer projects such as ramp builds, or raise money for home changes. Call 211 to find groups in South Carolina.

programs.name: South Carolina Department of Crime Victim Compensation
programs.federal_name: Crime Victims' Benefits (U.S. Department of Justice)
programs.about: South Carolina's crime victim compensation may help pay for home accessibility changes after an injury from a crime, when insurance or restitution does not cover it.

programs.name: Social Security Title XX Social Services (Social Services Block Grant)
programs.about: State human services offices use these federal funds for emergencies. For people already on public assistance, they can sometimes cover a ramp, rails or grab bars.

programs.name: South Carolina Workers' Compensation Commission
programs.about: If a work injury makes daily life at home hard, South Carolina workers' comp may pay for home changes or a move to a more suitable home.

programs.name: Internal Revenue Service: Personal Income Tax Deduction, Capital Gains Tax, Business Tax Deduction
State/Local Taxes: Sales Tax Exemption and Property Tax Exemption
programs.about: The lead list names no specific South Carolina credit. It notes that some states and counties exempt sales tax on accessibility items, and that home changes can raise assessed value. Check with the South Carolina revenue department and your county assessor.
